rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Graphical Method and Nature of Solutions
rows.stem: The pair of linear equations \(y = 0\) and \(y = -7\) have
rows.solution:
\(y = 0\) is the x-axis and \(y = -7\) is the line 7 units below it. Both are parallel to the x-axis, so the two lines never meet.

The pair has no solution, which is option (D) no solution.

rows.stem: The area of the square inscribed in a circle of radius \(5\sqrt{2}\) cm is :
rows.solution:
The diagonal of a square inscribed in a circle is a diameter, so the diagonal is \(2 \times 5\sqrt{2} = 10\sqrt{2}\) cm.

Side \(= \dfrac{10\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 10\) cm, so the area is \(10^2 = 100\ \text{cm}^2\), which is option (B) 100 cm\(^2\).

rows.subtopic: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: Two identical solid cubes of side ‘a’ are joined end-to-end. The total surface area of the resulting cuboid is :
rows.solution:
The resulting cuboid measures \(2a \times a \times a\).

Total surface area \(= 2(2a \cdot a + a \cdot a + a \cdot 2a) = 2(2a^2 + a^2 + 2a^2) = 10a^2\).

(Equivalently, the two cubes have \(12a^2\) of surface, and joining them hides one face of each: \(12a^2 - 2a^2 = 10a^2\).) This is option (B) \(10a^2\).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem: The probability of throwing a number greater than 2 with a fair die is :
rows.solution:
A die has 6 equally likely outcomes, and 4 of them (3, 4, 5, 6) are greater than 2.

\(P = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\), which is option (A) \(\dfrac{2}{3}\).

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: If \(y = 1\) is one of the solutions of the quadratic equation \(py^2 + py + 3 = 0\), then the value of p is :
rows.solution:
Since \(y = 1\) is a solution, \(p(1)^2 + p(1) + 3 = 0\), that is \(2p + 3 = 0\).

So \(p = -\dfrac{3}{2}\), which is option (C) \(-\dfrac{3}{2}\).

rows.stem: The value of \(\theta\) for which \(2\sin^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\); \(0^\circ \leq \theta \leq 90^\circ\) is :
rows.solution:
\(2\sin^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\) gives \(\sin^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{4}\). For \(0^\circ \le \theta \le 90^\circ\), \(\sin\theta \ge 0\), so \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(\theta = 30^\circ\).

This is option (A) \(30^\circ\).

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: In the given figure, \(\Delta ABC\) is circumscribing a circle. Find the length of BC, if AR = 4 cm, BR = 3 cm and AC = 11 cm.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the points of contact R (on AB), Q (on AC) and P (on BC) of the inscribed circle are named only in the drawing, which also marks AR = 4 cm, BR = 3 cm and AC = 11 cm. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
The circle touches AB at R, AC at Q and BC at P. Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.

From B: \(BP = BR = 3\) cm. From A: \(AQ = AR = 4\) cm.

So \(QC = AC - AQ = 11 - 4 = 7\) cm, and from C: \(PC = QC = 7\) cm.

\(BC = BP + PC = 3 + 7 = 10\) cm.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: A part of monthly hostel charges is fixed and the remaining depends on the number of days one has taken food in the mess. When a student A takes food for 20 days, she has to pay ₹ 1,500 as hostel charges while another student B, who takes food for 26 days, pays ₹ 1,800. Find the fixed charges and the cost of food.
rows.solution:
Let the fixed monthly charge be ₹ x and the cost of food be ₹ y per day.

\(x + 20y = 1500\) ... (i)

\(x + 26y = 1800\) ... (ii)

Subtracting (i) from (ii): \(6y = 300\), so \(y = 50\). Then \(x = 1500 - 20 \times 50 = 500\).

The fixed charge is ₹ 500 a month and the cost of food is ₹ 50 per day.

LHS \(= \sqrt{\sec^2\theta + \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta} = \sqrt{(1 + \tan^2\theta) + (1 + \cot^2\theta)}\).

Since \(\tan\theta\cot\theta = 1\), write \(2 = 2\tan\theta\cot\theta\):

LHS \(= \sqrt{\tan^2\theta + 2\tan\theta\cot\theta + \cot^2\theta} = \sqrt{(\tan\theta + \cot\theta)^2} = \tan\theta + \cot\theta =\) RHS.

(The positive root is taken, as \(\tan\theta + \cot\theta > 0\) for an acute angle \(\theta\).)

rows.stem:
The following distribution shows the daily pocket allowance of children of a locality. The mean daily pocket allowance is ₹ \(36{\cdot}10\). Find the missing frequency, f.

| Daily pocket allowance (in ₹) | 20 – 25 | 25 – 30 | 30 – 35 | 35 – 40 | 40 – 45 | 45 – 50 | 50 – 55 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of children | 7 | 6 | 9 | 13 | f | 5 | 4 |

The angles of depression of the top and the bottom of a 8 m tall building from the top of a multi-storeyed building are \(30^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\) respectively. Find the height of the multi-storeyed building and the distance between the two buildings.
rows.solution:
Let AB be the multi-storeyed building, H m high, and CD the 8 m building, with \(BD = x\) m the distance between them. Draw CE parallel to BD, meeting AB at E, so \(EC = x\) m and \(AE = (H - 8)\) m.

The angles of depression from A equal the angles of elevation at the other end (alternate angles): \(\angle ADB = 45^\circ\) and \(\angle ACE = 30^\circ\).

In right triangle ABD: \(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{H}{x} = 1\), so \(H = x\) ... (i)

In right triangle AEC: \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{H - 8}{x} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), so \(x = \sqrt{3}(H - 8)\) ... (ii)

From (i) and (ii): \(H = \sqrt{3}H - 8\sqrt{3}\), so \(H(\sqrt{3} - 1) = 8\sqrt{3}\) and

\(H = \dfrac{8\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{2} = 4(3 + \sqrt{3})\).

The height of the multi-storeyed building is \(4(3 + \sqrt{3})\) m, about \(18{\cdot}93\) m, and the distance between the two buildings is also \(4(3 + \sqrt{3})\) m, about \(18{\cdot}93\) m.
